subject: Lumina Diagnostics — Right-size recommendation and packaging options
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Lumina Diagnostics - initial right-size & packaging options

Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on the sample traffic you provided and our intake call, I pulled together two practical packaging options for Dedicated GPU capacity plus a short rationale for sizing. I attached the traffic CSV and a first-pass proposal (proposal_v1.xlsx). High level:

- Workload summary (from your sample): avg requests per minute = ~3,800; 95th percentile bursts ~6,200 rpm; median request has ~640 tokens input + 480 tokens output (chat-style back-and-forth). Typical context window required: up to 2,048 tokens for clinical summaries.
- Target latency goal: p95 generation latency <= 400ms for 1k contexts and sensible degradation for 2k contexts.
- Concurrency target: sustaining 60 concurrent live chat sessions during peak with burst headroom to 120 for short periods (5–10 minutes).

Recommendation (right-size): 5 x NVIDIA A10G-equivalent GPUs in a single reserved pool. Rationale: that configuration gives us the throughput to sustain 60 concurrent sessions at your average payload and handle p95 < 400ms for 1k contexts with ~25% operational headroom during sustained peaks. For the occasional high burst (the 6,000+ rpm spikes) we recommend a 2-GPU burst pool that bills at on-demand rates and autos-scales for short windows.

Packaging options (pricing is placeholder until finance signs off):
1) 12-month reserved commit (recommended) — reserve 5 GPUs; includes smart batching, prefix KV cache, and a 2-GPU burst pool. ~22% off on-demand for committed GPU-hours. SLA: 99.9% uptime on the pool layer, standard credits for downtime.
2) 24-month reserved commit — deeper discount (~30%) but requires annual payment. Also includes a complimentary 2-week runbook session with our SREs to optimize KV cache and batching.
3) Flex pilot — 3-month pilot with 3 reserved GPUs, ability to convert to a full commit at 60 days with retroactive discount.

Next steps: if this aligns, I’ll loop in Karthik to validate the performance math and Monica to start procurement paperwork and SOW. Also attached: Lumina_RFP_Attachments.pdf.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive

Emily — Sean —

Quick technical note to make the throughput math copy-paste friendly and to address quantization. I ran the numbers against your sample trace (thanks) and our internal perf profiles for Mistral-7B-like chat models (we use the model family as a conservative proxy):

Assumptions and measurements
- Average total tokens per request (in + out): 1,120 tokens
- Average generation tokens per request: 480 tokens
- Average encoder/context length: 640 tokens held in KV cache
- Average requests per minute (sustained peak): 3,800 rpm -> ~63 requests/sec sustained
- Concurrency target: 60 concurrent sessions approximates to ~60 active KV cache contexts.

Redwood perf estimates (A10G-equivalent):
- Single A10G sustained generation throughput: ~14 tokens/ms for the generator path (observed with batching and KV reuse patterns similar to your workload). That maps to ~32 concurrent low-latency chat streams for 480-token generations staying under 300–350ms p95 when batching is effective.
- With smart batching, KV cache sharing, and the observed request distribution, a 5-GPU pool yields sustained capacity for ~60 concurrent sessions with p95 ~350–420ms (1k context) and p95 ~550–700ms for 2k contexts in the worst case.

Headroom and burst handling
- We recommend the 2-GPU burst pool because your 95th-percentile minute-level spikes push the aggregate request rate >6k rpm and we'd rather route short bursts to the burst pool (cold-billed at on-demand) than over-provision the reserved pool. That pattern keeps committed costs lower while maintaining latency SLOs.

Quantization and quality impact
- INT8 quantization on our inference runtime typically improves throughput by ~20–35% depending on model shape and sequence length. For your clinical summarization models we expect ~25% throughput gains with negligible end-user quality regression after our recommended fine-tuning calibration step (we'll run a small eval suite). If you choose INT8 aggressively, you could downsize the pool by ~1 GPU in many cases, but we recommend validating on a holdout prompt set (we can run those evals during onboarding).

SLA / credits
- 99.9% uptime at pool-level equates to a credit of 10% of one month’s committed pool fees for each month the SLA is missed (standard clause). Scheduled maintenance windows are excluded if we provide 72-hour notice; emergency maintenance is handled case-by-case (we include a 2-hour failover to burst pool where applicable).

If you want, I can include the succinct bullet list above in an SOW section for your infra runbook.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
